group.title: Housework
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: An electric machine that sucks dust and dirt off floors and carpets.
examples: I use the {vacuum cleaner} on the carpet every Saturday.
wrong: She washed the plates in the vacuum cleaner.

words.meaning: The bowl in a kitchen or bathroom with taps, where you wash things.
examples: Put the dirty cups in the {sink}.
wrong: We keep the sink in the garden next to the trees.

words.meaning: A container where you put things you throw away.
examples: Throw the paper in the {trash can}.
wrong: I keep my clean clothes in the trash can.

words.meaning: An open round container with a handle for carrying water.
examples: Fill the {bucket} with warm water and soap.
wrong: The bucket has a lid and no handle, so you carry it in your pocket.

words.meaning: A soft thing full of small holes that takes in water, used for washing.
examples: Wipe the table with a wet {sponge}.
wrong: The sponge was so hard that it broke the window.

words.meaning: To rub something so that it becomes clean and shiny.
examples: Dad {polished} his shoes before the party.
wrong: She polished the table until it was dull and dirty.

words.meaning: A tool with a heavy metal head used for hitting nails.
examples: Pass me the {hammer} so I can put up this picture.
wrong: He cut the bread with a hammer.

words.meaning: A thin pointed piece of metal you hit into wood to hold things.
examples: I hung the clock on a {nail} in the wall.
wrong: The nail is soft and made of paper.

words.meaning: A tool for turning screws to put them in or take them out.
examples: Use a {screwdriver} to open the back of the radio.
wrong: She stirred her soup with a screwdriver.

words.meaning: Two long pieces joined by steps, used to climb up high.
examples: He climbed the {ladder} to clean the windows.
wrong: We used the ladder to go down into the bath.

words.meaning: A thing you hold in your hand to help you make or fix something.
examples: My uncle keeps every {tool} in a red box.
wrong: A tool is something you eat for breakfast.

words.meaning: The glass part of a lamp that gives light.
examples: The kitchen is dark because the {light bulb} is broken.
wrong: I changed the light bulb, so now the room has no light.

words.meaning: A small oven that heats food very quickly.
examples: Heat the soup in the {microwave} for two minutes.
wrong: I keep the ice cream frozen in the microwave.

words.meaning: The kitchen machine with places on top for cooking food in pans.
examples: The pasta is boiling on the {stove}.
wrong: We sleep on the stove because it is soft.

words.meaning: A pot with a spout and handle for boiling water.
examples: Put the {kettle} on and I’ll make some tea.
wrong: She used the kettle to keep the milk cold.

words.meaning: A flat metal pan with a long handle, used for cooking eggs and meat.
examples: He cooked two eggs in the {frying pan}.
wrong: I drank my coffee from the frying pan.

words.meaning: A deep round metal pot with a handle, used for cooking on top of a stove.
examples: Boil the rice in a small {saucepan}.
wrong: The saucepan is a flat plate for serving cake.

words.meaning: A small electric machine that makes bread brown and hot.
examples: Put two slices of bread in the {toaster}.
wrong: The toaster keeps bread cold and fresh.

words.meaning: A very cold box or part of a fridge that keeps food frozen.
examples: There is ice cream in the {freezer}.
wrong: Put the bread in the freezer to make it warm.

words.meaning: A flat piece of wood or plastic you cut food on.
examples: Chop the onions on the {cutting board}.
wrong: We hung the cutting board on the wall as a mirror.

words.meaning: A piece of cloth you wear over your clothes to keep them clean when cooking.
examples: Wear an {apron} so you don’t get sauce on your shirt.
wrong: He wore an apron so his clothes got dirty.

words.meaning: A flat board with low edges for carrying food and drinks.
examples: She brought the cups in on a {tray}.
wrong: He carried the soup on a tray with holes in it.

words.meaning: To cut something into thin flat pieces.
examples: Can you {slice} the tomatoes for the salad?
wrong: She sliced the bread into one big round ball.

words.meaning: A dirty mark that is hard to remove.
examples: There’s a coffee {stain} on my white shirt.
wrong: The stain made the shirt look cleaner than before.

words.meaning: A tool that turns fast to make holes in walls or wood.
examples: Use the {drill} to make a hole for the shelf.
wrong: He used a drill to fill the holes in the wall.

words.meaning: When a liquid falls in small drops.
examples: Water {drips} from the old kitchen tap all night.
wrong: The tap dripped so much that the sink stayed completely dry.

words.meaning: Letting water or air get out through a small hole.
examples: The {leaky} tap drips all night.
wrong: The roof is leaky, so the room stays dry in the rain.

words.meaning: Clean and in good order.
examples: Her room is always very {neat}.
wrong: His desk was neat, with papers and food all over it.

words.meaning: A thin metal pin with a twisting edge that you turn into wood.
examples: Tighten the {screw} so the shelf doesn’t fall.
wrong: He ate the screw with a spoon.

words.meaning: To wash the plates, cups and pans after a meal.
examples: You cooked, so I’ll {do the dishes}.
wrong: He did the dishes, so the plates are still dirty.

words.meaning: To carry the bags of rubbish outside to the bins.
examples: Please {take out the trash} before it smells.
wrong: He took out the trash and put it back under the sink.

words.meaning: To wash dirty clothes, sheets and towels.
examples: I {do the laundry} on Sunday afternoons.
wrong: She did the laundry, so all her clothes are dirty.

words.meaning: The job of making clothes smooth with a hot iron.
examples: There is a big pile of {ironing} on the chair.
wrong: Ironing makes your shirts full of lines.

words.meaning: To put something back in the place where it is kept.
examples: {Put away} your toys before dinner.
wrong: He put away the plates by leaving them on the floor.

words.meaning: A thick glove you wear to hold hot pans.
examples: Use an {oven mitt} to take the tray out.
wrong: I wore an oven mitt to keep my hands cold in the snow.

words.meaning: A flat container you sweep dirt into from the floor.
examples: Sweep the crumbs into the {dustpan}.
wrong: He drank water from the dustpan.

words.meaning: A piece of soft material for cleaning or drying things.
examples: Wipe the table with a damp {cloth}.
wrong: The cloth is made of hard metal.

words.meaning: A strong chemical liquid used to clean and make things white.
examples: She cleans the toilet with {bleach}.
wrong: Bleach is safe to drink with your lunch.

words.meaning: Gloves that keep your hands dry when you wash or clean.
examples: Put on {rubber gloves} before you clean the bathroom.
wrong: She wore rubber gloves to get her hands wet.

words.meaning: A liquid you add to water to wash plates and pans.
examples: Add a little {dish soap} to the hot water.
wrong: She washed her hair with dish soap and a hammer.
